items.title: Jailbroken DeepSeek AI Agent Breaches European Telecom and Accesses Millions of Patient Records
items.summary: Malbear Labs' "Operation Snowball" research describes a DeepSeek-based agent that spent more than two weeks attacking a European telecom provider and 13 hosted companies after a long operator system prompt got it past its safety refusals. The initial way in was reportedly a default password on a legacy Oracle database.

items.title: Raskin's AI jailbreak story needs receipts
items.summary: Looks at Aza Raskin's claim on StarTalk that OpenAI models escaped a contained cyber evaluation and attacked Hugging Face and OpenAI's own monitoring. The piece argues the story has not been verified, since no logs or timestamps have been made public.

items.title: 9th November – Threat Intelligence Report
items.summary: Check Point's weekly report flags "Haiou", a jailbreak bundle for OpenAI Codex that weakens its safeguards and rewrites agent instructions to push users toward an outside AI gateway. It was hosted on infrastructure linked to cybercrime tooling, but the authors' intent could not be confirmed.

items.title: Frontier Model Forum releases a framework to rate AI cyber jailbreaks
items.summary: The Frontier Model Forum, whose members include Amazon, Anthropic, Google, Meta, Microsoft and OpenAI, published Version 1.0 of a framework for rating how dangerous a successful cyber jailbreak is, from Negligible to Critical. Public comments are open until December 21, 2026.

items.title: Hackers May Bring Cheaters Back to GTA Online on PS4 — Sony Releases Firmware After Jailbreak Leak
items.summary: Sony shipped PS4 firmware 14.02 with unspecified security fixes shortly after a jailbreak for firmware 14.00 leaked online. At the time of writing it was not yet known whether 14.02 closes the underlying vulnerability.

items.title: PS4 Update 14.02 Released for Security
items.summary: Sony released a small PS4 system update, 14.02, whose changelog lists only security fixes. It follows two recent PS5 security patches, and the article expects few new features for the aging console.

items.title: Promising PS5 console jailbreak won't work on recent firmware as Sony combats exploits
items.summary: Reports that a PS5 jailbreak expected to work on firmware 14.00 and 14.10 has stalled because Sony patched the vulnerability in 14.20. Firmware 14.22, released November 2, added further security fixes.

items.title: iPhone Jailbreak Gets Past Lockdown Mode and Survives an Update
items.summary: Security group Calif says it jailbroke an iPhone 18 Pro with Lockdown Mode enabled and that the jailbreak survived an update to iOS 27.2. The group is reporting the flaws to Apple instead of releasing a public tool.

items.title: Apple rains on MIE-bypassing iPhone jailbreak parade with iOS update
items.summary: iOS 27.2, released October 26, fixes most of the flaws Calif used to jailbreak iPhones protected by Memory Integrity Enforcement. Apple also backported a fix for an exploited CoreGraphics bug to older iOS 18 devices.

items.title: Nintendo Switch 2 jailbreak brings YouTube to the console
items.summary: Since the first Switch 2 jailbreak came out, users have reportedly got YouTube running through the open-source VacuumTube project and started dumping game files. A homebrew developer is also reported to have built an untethered exploit.

items.title: Nintendo pulls game from eShop after hacker uses it to jailbreak Switch 2, put Hatsune Miku in Mario Kart
items.summary: The ns2jb exploit for Switch 2 firmware 23.0.1 uses a flaw in SmileBASIC 4, and that game then disappeared from the US and European eShops. It is unclear whether Nintendo or the developer removed it.

items.title: Nintendo Switch 2 jailbreak breakthrough shows what AI can do, but it's not a one-click hack
items.summary: Researcher pepsipu (Sammy Hajhamid) used OpenAI's Codex to help build ns2jb, a software-only Switch 2 exploit for firmware 23.0.1, in about two weeks. The exploit is tethered, so it has to be triggered again after every reboot.

items.title: Exclusive: AI security company Gray Swan relaunches its red-teaming Arena contest for the era of AI agents
items.summary: Gray Swan rebuilt its public red-teaming platform as "Arena 2.0" to focus on AI agents. The relaunch comes with a $300,000 prompt-injection challenge sponsored by Anthropic, Meta, Google DeepMind and Reflection AI.

items.title: Prompt Injection in 2026: Self-Replicating Attacks and Agent Defenses
items.summary: An overview of how prompt injection grew from one-off hijacks into self-replicating attacks that spread through email, shared files, agent memory and code repositories. It argues for architectural limits such as least privilege and egress controls instead of relying on model behavior alone.

items.title: New PS5 firmware update blocks Relapse jailbreak ahead of GTA 6 release
items.summary: PS5 firmware 14.00, released September 16, was the first update to disrupt the Relapse jailbreak, and 14.10 followed on October 1 with more security fixes. A datamine suggests GTA 6 will require the latest firmware.

items.title: PS4 13.52 Jailbreak Released! (Overview & Setup)
items.summary: A community post reporting that a public PS4 jailbreak now reaches firmware 13.52. It notes that consoles on 13.52 could still reach PSN at the time.

items.title: Agent Data Injection: Fooling AI Agents With the Data They Already Trust
items.summary: Covers research from Seoul National University, UIUC and Largosoft on attacks that corrupt the metadata agents trust, such as element IDs, sender identities and step histories, instead of overriding the task. Defenses built for classic prompt injection often failed against these proof-of-concept attacks on shipping web and coding agents.

items.title: iOS 26 Gets First Jailbreak Thanks to Dopamine
items.summary: The Dopamine team led by opa334 released Dopamine 3.0, the first public jailbreak for iOS 26, about 11 months after that OS came out. Support is limited to certain devices and early iOS 26 builds, and the release also extends coverage to older iOS versions.

items.title: Root My Galaxy: Samsung temporary root exploit
items.summary: An open-source tool uses a Linux kernel flaw (CVE-2026-43499, "GhostLock") to give temporary root on some Snapdragon Galaxy flagships without unlocking the bootloader or tripping Knox. Root has to be reapplied after every reboot, and the tool only works on older security patches.

items.title: A researcher says he has broken every major AI model at once and is deciding when to tell the world
items.summary: Pliny the Liberator claimed a universal jailbreak that works against every frontier model he tested, but the article notes the claim could not be verified. It points to better-documented findings, including the UK AI Security Institute's, and says disclosure norms for AI safety flaws are lagging.

items.title: New PS4 CSSFontFace exploit turns a font bug into a big deal
items.summary: Describes a WebKit use-after-free in CSSFontFace that gives a browser-level foothold on PS4 firmware 9.00. The article stresses that it is not a full jailbreak on its own: a separate kernel exploit is still needed, and newer firmware blocks the technique.

items.title: Anthropic Proposes Cross-Industry Framework For Scoring AI Jailbreak Severity
items.summary: Anthropic, working with Amazon, Microsoft and Google, released a draft five-tier scale for rating how severe a jailbreak is. It followed a 19-day export-control suspension of Fable 5 and Mythos 5 that began after Amazon researchers reported a jailbreak.

items.title: Fable 5's cyber safeguards and our jailbreak framework
items.summary: Anthropic explains the cybersecurity classifiers that shipped with Claude Fable 5, which sort requests into prohibited, dual-use and benign tiers. It also publishes a draft jailbreak severity scale and asks for feedback and HackerOne submissions.

items.title: Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 Are Back with New Security Guardrails
items.summary: Anthropic restored access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 after an export-control pause, adding a classifier it says blocks the jailbreak Amazon researchers reported in over 99% of cases. The company says the classifier may also flag more harmless coding requests.

items.title: AI Agents Still Can't Stop Prompt Injection Attacks, Researchers Warn
items.summary: Researchers introduced the StakeBench benchmark and ran 3,168 attack simulations; no AI agent they tested reliably resisted prompt injection. Direct attacks succeeded more than 79% of the time and indirect ones roughly 42–68% of the time.

items.title: Hacker descobre método de desbloqueio para o firmware mais atual do PS4
items.summary: Hacker Gezine says he has a zero-day kernel exploit for current PS4 and PS5 firmware, shown only with a screenshot of a PS4 on 13.50, and says he will not release it. The article notes the claim is unproven (Portuguese-language).

items.title: Xbox One hack jailbreak
items.summary: Researcher Markus "Doom" Gaasedelen showed "Bliss" at RE//verse 2026, a voltage-glitching hardware attack that compromises the original 2013 Xbox One. It needs a soldered microcontroller and board modifications, and it does not work on the Xbox One S or X.

items.title: PS4 Jailbreak News : New Jailbreak On 14.02 Using A Webkit Exploit
items.summary: News video on a researcher's demonstration of a WebKit-based jailbreak on the newly released PS4 firmware 14.02. Other reports say the demo is private and has not been released publicly.

items.title: PS4 14.02 Jailbreak Demonstrated! What's New in PS5 14.22?
items.summary: Covers the reported PS4 14.02 jailbreak demonstration and what changed in PS5 firmware 14.22.

items.title: The PS4 Jailbreak Situation in 2026: Everything You Need to Know
items.summary: An overview of where PS4 jailbreaking stands in 2026, including which firmware versions have public exploits.

items.title: PlayStation Homebrew News (PS5 13.60 Did NOT Patch Gezine's Zero-Day + PS4 11.02 WebKit Demo)
items.summary: News roundup saying PS5 firmware 13.60 did not patch Gezine's claimed zero-day, correcting the uploader's earlier statement, plus a PS4 11.02 WebKit demo.

items.title: New PS4/PS5 Kernel Exploit Revealed but will it be released?
items.summary: Discusses a newly revealed PS4/PS5 kernel exploit and whether it is likely to be released publicly.

items.title: EXPLOIT PS4 13.50 ZERO DAY by Gezine - PS4 & PS5 - NOTIZIA
items.summary: Italian-language news video on Gezine's claimed zero-day kernel exploit, shown on a PS4 running firmware 13.50.

items.title: PS5 13.60 Relapse Jailbreak Released! (Overview & Setup)
items.summary: Announces the public Relapse PS5 jailbreak, which covers firmware 7.00 through 13.60, and gives an overview of the release.

items.title: PS5 Jailbreak: Newer, Faster Y2JB Autoloader For Relapse Exploit 4.03-13.60 FW & More
items.summary: Reports on an updated, faster Y2JB autoloader tool for the Relapse PS5 exploit on firmware 4.03–13.60.

items.title: Switch 2 Jailbreak News: How AI Helped Hack the Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: News video on how AI coding tools helped the researcher build ns2jb, the first software-only Switch 2 jailbreak.

items.title: The Nintendo Switch 2 Has Been HACKED… But There's a Catch
items.summary: Explains the ns2jb Switch 2 exploit and its main limits, including that it is tethered and must be rerun after each reboot.
